title: Hollowness of Safdie Films (uncut gems/good times)

commenti.body: [removed]
[removed]

I think it’s due to the nature of the main characters of each story- they’re both pushing their luck and digging themselves into a deeper and deeper hole. If you go into the movies expecting to be thrilled by watching the main characters overcoming obstacles and winning, you’ll be disappointed. I think the thrill and appeal is difficult to grasp. However, I do think Howie’s big win at the end of Uncut Gems is incredibly satisfying to watch. 
I think of them in narrative terms. It’s less like a Hero’s Journey, and more like a tragedy, or a Rise-and-Fall of a character. 

I also think that Daniel Lopatin’s score has a lot to do with how “satisfying” these are to watch.

Uncut Gem is superbly immersive. The shaky and fast pace I am witnessing is exactly what the main character is going through. The events are non stop, and the camera is shaky. I enjoy being overwhelmed and worn down by the movie because it fits the theme.

I agree with you OP, even though we are almost certainly in the minority. There’s a difference between tension and stress. Uncut Gems is stressful, but there’s no tension. That atmosphere  became grating and boring after a while. But different strokes for different folks.

They're character studies. I suspect you're approaching the films from a plot sense.

Cassavetes films don't have particular scenes which in themselves are gripping, but saying "What could Cassavetes have done better" would get you expelled from film school.

Immerse yourselves in the struggles of the characters, not the scenes.

I think these movies are completely vapid, however: that´s why they´re also maybe mildly important, quite representational of the times.... but how such a big audience can enjoy them is beyond me. Uncut Gems was a little bit better than Good Times, but I felt this was mainly because of Sandler´s ´better acting chops than usual´ and the ´woha he´s in it´-factor, which, for me, became almost the focal point of the movie, after being bombarded with it on the internet.
Stylistically I think the director duo has talent, though I don´t think a shaky camera and saturated coloring is necessary to convey everyday horror. Far from it even. On that front I think it shows their immature nature.

I'm with you guys. Uncut Gems is like if ADHD was a movie. I'm glad to know I didn't miss out on anything resembling meaning by turning it off halfway through.

Yea I think you hit the nail on the head. The tension is lacking despite their being well maintained stress level.
I feel like the first hour or so of the film could’ve been shortened with just some  fast paced cut scenes to give you a backstory on him. It sorte felt like an elongated version of that anyway.

I think your first point is interesting. I imagine this movie garnered an audience (due to Sandler) that normally wouldn’t watch a more indie style movie that doesn’t have a marvel-level archetypal plot arc.

These films are a classic example of style over substance. The director is focused on creating a grungy atmosphere and aesthetic above all else (and one that doesn't actually feel very believable to those who've spent time in this environment). For the viewer , it's an exercise in putting up with an incessant , claustrophobic , deeply depressing mood - one without any particular sympathetic characters or moments of light and shade. 

Unlike a film like "Kids" which accurately portrays the chaos, complexity of the city and creates characters that are believable, flawed yet sympathetic - Safdie's characters are frequently mean spirited and selfish and lack the kind of depth that can make them believable. His films are hollow because they are like an Instagram filter - they use colours , editing and dialogue to create a mood that is actually pretty unpleasant and exhausting - but beyond that , they don't have the soul or the spirit to capture life and characters in a way that goes beyond merely the aesthetic. A product of our age that prioritizes the surface (and a film / critic industy that rewards that as 'edgy' and  'challenging')
How does one distinguish style from substance?

Yup. It’s that lack of soul that is hard to place that is just lacking for me to be completely drawn into this world and the characters.
The aesthetic is there but you’re still left unconvinced and I think it’s bc it does not fully convince you the events/people are real

I like Good Time & don't like Uncut Gems. My issue with Uncut Gems is that it's so static, energy-wise. It maintains the same energy level and atmosphere throughout the whole film, there are no breaks or variations in it, and so it just starts to feel monotonous by the end. I like Good Time because it has more variation in the pacing & energy.

My issue with both films, though, is that they have a real edge lord quality to them. At the end of both of them, it feels like the Safdies are saying "Yeah, that was pretty DARK wasn't it?! I bet you can't believe how despicable some people can be!!" It just feels like the main goal is to shock you — and to your point, that's an empty and hollow reason for a movie to exist.

I grew up in the northeast and I knew so many people like Robert Pattinson's character in Good Time as a teen (not to mention the Ray character, Jesus). 

I find the Safdie's character work and dialogue to be so authentic that it's wild to see someone accusing them of trying to be edgy

It's not that the character work and dialogue is trying to be edgy, but rather, that the broader story they are telling is an attempt to be edgy. I enjoy Good Time, but at its core, I don't think there's much there other than "look at how dark and depraved these characters are!"

Hard disagree, I think there are a lot of film makers who do that shit but Safdie’s are one of them. To me it’s watching someone with the most misguided and destructive love pathologically lie and steal his way toward his helping his brother, but only ACTUALLY helping his brother when he is stopped and caged at the end.


There’s a ton there under the surface imo, same with uncut gems
That's an interesting read on the movie and I'm gonna think about that next time I watch it, thank you.

I’ve only seen Good Time once but Uncut Gems is a personal favorite. I was neutral about Good Time. All the qualities are there that explain why the Safdies Bros have been called up to the big leagues but I didn’t personally connect with it. My response to Uncut Gems the first time was, a bit like you, what a wild ride. I enjoyed the ride though and saw it two or three times in theaters.

I’ve since purchased it and it’s become a favorite. I would suggest rewatching it. I view Uncut Gems as a deeply American film. Howie is from the jump a deeply flawed man and played by any number of other great actors he probably doesn’t earn the audiences bond. But Sandler is perfect for the role. In his early comedies he was often the heel and he is here again. Kind of like a little boy pretending to be a man. I am deeply moved by the end of that film. It feels like one of the best tragedies to come out of recent years. Howie is like a bizarro world George Bailey, personally at fault for potentially ruining his families life, but so driven by his addiction that, in this moment, for now, he wins. There’s a way that film could have ended where that kind of “lesson” is given to the audience at the end. “He got away with it this time.” But in killing him we actually experience the high of his victory in more sharpened relief. This is a trashy human, but we now understand a bit of how this all makes him feel.

Having seen the description of their potential next film, I am curious what else they have within them because it sounds a lot like their previous movies. But on its own Uncut Gems is deeply moving. Perhaps if you rewatch with some time in between viewings, without the frantic anxiety, you’ll be able to experience some of those textures

I don’t know. There are people like these characters. There’s a seediness to their films that might be more artifice than observed but this is the kind of world they grew up in. I think when some kids raise themselves it’s hard to imagine that from the outside. They seem like they raised themselves
